newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Merrill says CRT sale shows Brazil telecoms cheap.
newsitem.headline: Merrill says CRT sale shows Brazil telecoms cheap.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co. said the sale of a minority stake in Rio Grande do Sul state's telecom for 681 million reais, 54.8 percent above base price, highlights how cheap Brazilian telecom stocks are.
"This validates our long-held view that Brazilian telephone stocks are woefully undervalued and that they will appreciate substantially as privatization approaches," the brokerage said in a report.
The government plans to break up and sell off federal telecoms giant Telebras and its 27 subsidiaries, probably starting next year with Sao Paulo unit Telesp and long-distance subsidiary Embratel.
"We strongly encourage long-term investors to buy and hold the shares of Telebras and its subsidiaries," the brokerage said.
A group including Telefonica de Espana and Brazil's RBS, offered Tuesday the winning bid for 35 percent of voting shares in CRT, known formally as Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes.

Merrill said the price offered by the RBS-Telefonica group equals $3,800 per access line. That figure "compares to current public market values of $2,191 and $2,740 per line for Telebras and Telesp respectively," it added.
Merrill said it has set a 12-month price target for Telebras of $95 and a price target of $240 for Telesp preferred shares.
"When privatization is complete, we estimate the break-up value of Telebras' component parts at $140 per share," it said.

Telebras' ADR closed at 76 7/8 in New York while its preferred and common shares ended at 79.30 reais and 72.70 reais respectively Thursday in Sao Paulo. Telesp preferred closed at 227 reais on the local bourse.
